chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
question_text: Is it necessary that a mass should be present at the centre of mass of any system?

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 7 VERY SHORT ANSWER. The 1+1 mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for this question, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The answer

lines.text: No. Mass need not be present at the

lines: centre of mass of a system.
steps.margin_note: Answer "no" in the first line. The centre of mass is a mathematical point, not a particle.
steps.why: The centre of mass is the average POSITION of the mass, weighted by how much mass sits where. An average need not land on any actual object.
common_mistakes: Answering yes because the name contains the word "mass".

recall.must_convey: That no, mass need not be present at the centre of mass.
accept: no, mass need not be present
centre of mass can be empty
reject: a ring has its centre of mass at its centre

steps.memory_tip: No — the centre of mass is an AVERAGE position, and an average need not be occupied.

steps.label: The example
lines: Example: a uniform ring. Its centre of
mass is at its geometric centre, where
there is no material at all.
steps.margin_note: The ring is the expected example — one line names it, one line says why it works.
steps.why: Every particle of the ring sits on the rim, yet symmetry places the average of all of them exactly at the empty centre.
common_mistakes: Giving a solid sphere as the example — its centre of mass has material at it, so it proves nothing.

recall.must_convey: That a uniform ring has its centre of mass at its empty centre.
accept: centre of mass of a ring is at the centre where there is no mass
ring ki centre lo mass undadu
reject: no, mass need not be present

steps.memory_tip: The ring: all its mass is on the rim, yet the centre of mass is at the empty centre.

insider_note: The one-word answer "No" earns only the first mark. The second is the example, so the ring has to be written down.
